rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because believers were harmed by polytheists, God gives them worldly good news by hastening punishment for the disbelievers, the enemies of believers.
rows.anchor: فعجل الله لهم البشرى في الدنيا بعقاب الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In anger or distress, people pray for harm against themselves and their families as rashly as they pray for good, although they would not want the harmful prayer answered.
rows.anchor: يدعو في حال الضجر والغضب على نفسه وأهله بما لا يحب ان يستجاب له

rows.speaker: الزجاج وغيره
rows.claim: The human here is generic: the verse refers to people as a class.
rows.anchor: انه اسم جنس يراد به الناس قاله الزجاج وغيره

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The human is Adam, whose mention stands for his descendants.
rows.anchor: آدم فاكتفى بذكره من ذكر ولده ذكره ابن الأنباري

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The human is al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who asked for stones to rain from heaven.
rows.anchor: قاله مقاتل وقال سلمان الفارسي أول ما خلق الله من آدم

rows.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
rows.claim: Adam hurried God to finish creating him when only his legs remained; this explains the description of humans as hasty.
rows.anchor: قال سلمان الفارسي أول ما خلق الله من آدم رأسه فجعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day are two signs that point to the power of their Creator.
rows.anchor: أي علامتين يدلان على قدرة خالقهما

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام وابن عباس في آخرين
rows.claim: The erased sign of night is the moon, whose dark markings are the erasure.
rows.anchor: آية الليل القمر ومحوها ما في بعض القمر من الاسوداد والى هذا المعنى ذهب علي عليه السلام وابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The night sign was erased by the darkness made constant in night, since darkness removes and extinguishes lights.
rows.anchor: آية الليل محيت بالظلمة التي جعلت ملازمة لليل فنسب المحو إلى الظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says sun and moon once had equal brightness, then Gabriel swept his wing over the moon and extinguished its light.
rows.anchor: ويروى ان الشمس والقمر كانا في النور والضوء سواء فأرسل الله جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The daylight sign means the sun, and the readings of mubṣira offer three closely related explanations.
rows.anchor: يعني الشمس مبصرة فيه ثلاثة أقوال

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Mubṣira means luminous; Ibn al-Anbari says describing a sign as seeing is figurative usage.
rows.anchor: منيرة قاله قتادة قال ابن الانباري وانما صلح وصف الاية بالابصار على جهة المجاز

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Mubṣira means that people see by means of it.
rows.anchor: ان معنى مبصرة مبصرا بها قاله ابن قتيبة

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Mubṣira can mean that daylight makes people see and shows them things; the explanations are close in meaning.
rows.anchor: ان معنى مبصرة مبصرة فجرى مفعل مجرى مفعل والمعنى انها تبصر الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daylight lets people see how to go about their work and seek their provision.
rows.anchor: لتبصروا كيف تتصرفون في أعمالكم وتطلبون رزقكم بالنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Erasing the night sign makes it possible to count years and reckon time; otherwise night and day and their number would not be distinguishable.
rows.anchor: بمحو آية الليل ولولا ذلك لم يعرف الليل من النهار ولم يتبين العدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has explained everything people need so clearly that it cannot be confused with something else.
rows.anchor: بيناه تبينا لا يلتبس معه بغيره

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: He reads kullu with the lām nominative rather than accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة وكل برفع اللام

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبي والحسن
rows.claim: They read ṭāʾir as ṭayri, with yāʾ and without alif.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وأبي والحسن ألزمناه طيره بياء ساكنة من غير الف

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: One view identifies a person's allotted bird with their misery or felicity.
rows.anchor: شقاوته وسعادته قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says every newborn has a leaf around its neck marked either wretched or happy.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد ما من مولود يولد إلا وفي عنقه ورقة مكتوب فيها شقي أو سعيد

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the bird signifies a person's deeds; al-Hasan is also reported to hold both this and the preceding view.
rows.anchor: عمله قاله الفراء وعن الحسن كالقولين

rows.speaker: خصيف
rows.claim: A further view takes the bird as whatever befalls a person; Abu Ubayda glosses it as one's allotted share.
rows.anchor: انه ما يصيبه قاله خصيف وقال أبو عبيدة حظه

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains it as each person's divinely allotted share of good and evil, which remains bound to that person; bird language echoes Arab omens.
rows.anchor: لكل امرئ حظا من الخير والشر قد قضاه الله عليه فهو لازم عنقه

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: The Qur'an addresses Arabs in their own omen idiom, teaching that what they assign to a bird is actually attached to their own necks.
rows.anchor: فخاطبهم الله بما يستعملون واعلمهم ان ذلك الأمر الذي يجعلونه بالطائر هو الذي يلزمه أعناقهم

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: God knew and recorded Adam's obedient and disobedient descendants, decreeing felicity for the first and misery for the second; each person's destiny is fixed at creation.
rows.anchor: علم المطيع من ذريته والعاصي فكتب ما علمه منهم اجمعين وقضى سعادة من علمه مطيعا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The bird can mean the person's deeds from which people themselves would take omens; neck signifies that the deeds remain attached to them.
rows.anchor: ما يتطير من مثله من شيء عمله وذكر العنق عبارة عن اللزوم له

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The Arabs called deeds birds because they used to take omens from certain actions.
rows.anchor: الاصل في تسميتهم العمل طائرا انهم كانوا يتطيرون من بعض الاعمال

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: He reads the passive verb yukhraju with yāʾ, ḍamma, and fatḥ on the rāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ويخرج بياء مضمومة وفتح الراء

rows.speaker: يعقوب وعبد الوارث
rows.claim: They read yukhraju with open yāʾ and ḍamma on the rāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب وعبد الوارث بالياء مفتوحة وضم الراء

rows.speaker: قتادة وأبو المتوكل
rows.claim: They read yukhraju with nominative yāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قتادة وابو المتوكل ويخرج بياء مرفوعة وكسر الراء

rows.speaker: أبو الجوزاء والأعرج
rows.claim: They read the verb with an open tāʾ and nominative rāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو الجوزاء والأعرج وتخرج بتاء مفتوحة ورفع الراء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك
rows.claim: They read kitāb in the nominative rather than accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك كتاب بالرفع

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: They read yulaqqāhu with ḍamma on the yāʾ and a doubled qāf.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وابو جعفر يلقاه بضم الياء وتشديد القاف

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They incline the qāf in yulaqqāhu.
rows.anchor: وامال حمزة والكسائي القاف

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The book is the record of a person's deeds.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون هذا كتابه الذي فيه ما عمل

rows.speaker: أبو السوار العدوي
rows.claim: He likens the record to an open page during life, folded at death, and opened again at resurrection, urging people to write what they wish while alive.
rows.anchor: فصحيفتك منشورة فأمل فيها ما شئت فاذا مت طويت ثم اذا بعثت نشرت

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: He reads iqraʾ with a light hamza; the construction omits the understood phrase, meaning the person is told to read the book.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر اقرأ بتخفيف الهمزة وفيه اضمار تقديره فيقال له اقرأ كتابك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Everyone will read the record, whether or not they were literate in life.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن يقرؤه أميا كان أو غير أمي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The one who made a person account for himself has dealt justly with him.
rows.anchor: ولقد عدل عليك من جعلك حسيب نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥasīb has three interpretations: one who reckons, a witness, or one who suffices.
rows.anchor: وفي معنى حسيبا ثلاثة اقوال احدها محاسبا والثاني شاهدا والثالث كافيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Self-accounting lets a person see God's justice, the proof against them, and why punishment is deserved; entry to Paradise is by God's grace, while entry to Hell is because of one's own sin.
rows.anchor: ليعلم عدل الله بين العباد ويرى وجوب حجة الله عليه واستحقاقه العقوبة

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The masculine ḥasīban with feminine nafs is explained by meaning the person, or because nafs has no visible feminine marker and resembles nouns such as sky and earth.
rows.anchor: وانما قال حسيبا والنفس مؤنثة لأنه يعني بالنفس الشخص أو لأنه لا علامة للتأنيث في لفظ النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic poetry likewise uses a masculine predicate with earth, cited as a parallel to the grammatical construction.
rows.anchor: ولا أرض ابقل ابقالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who is guided receives the reward of guidance, while the penalty for error falls on the person who strays.
rows.anchor: له ثواب اهتدائه وعليه عقاب ضلاله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra told people to follow him because he would carry their sins; the verse denies that one soul can bear another's burden.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ان الوليد بن المغير قال اتبعوني

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: The phrase means that no sinful soul incurs another soul's sin; wazara is explained as sinning or bearing sin.
rows.anchor: ولا تأثم آثمة إثم أخرى قال الزجاج يقال وزر يزر فهو وازر وزرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may mean either that no sinner is punished for another's sin, or that one should not sin merely because someone else did so, as the disbelievers appealed to their ancestors.
rows.anchor: والثاني أنه لا ينبغي أن يعمل الإنسان بالإثم لأن غيره عمله كما قال الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger must clarify what brings punishment and what leads to Paradise before God punishes people.
rows.anchor: حتى نبين ما به نعذب وما من اجله ندخل الجنة

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
rows.claim: The verse supports the view that knowing God is not rationally obligatory but becomes obligatory through revealed law and the sending of messengers; one who dies before that is not definitively judged for Hell.
rows.anchor: معرفة الله لا تجب عقلا وإنما تجب بالشرع وهو بعثة الرسل وانه لو مات الإنسان قبل ذلك لم يقطع عليه بالنار

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
rows.claim: Alternatively, punishment in matters known only through revelation requires a messenger's proof; a convert in enemy territory need not make up rites unheard of there.
rows.anchor: لا يعذب في ما طريقه السمع الا بقيام حجة السمع من جهة الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Qubāʾ turned toward the Kaaba without restarting the prayer, illustrating that a ruling not previously heard does not require repetition.
rows.anchor: قصة أهل قباء حين استداروا إلى الكعبة ولم يستأنفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A convert in Muslim territory who had not learned that prayer was obligatory must make up prayers because public prayer, calls, and congregations made the duty apparent.
rows.anchor: لأنه قد رأى الناس يصلون في المساجد بأذان وإقامة وذلك دعاء اليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two explanations are given for God's intention to destroy a town: its prior decree of misery, or its people's obstinacy toward and denial of the prophets.
rows.anchor: في سبب ارادته لذلك قولان احدهما ما سبق لهم في قضائه من الشقاء والثاني عنادهم الانبياء وتكذيبهم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: On the majority reading, the command to its affluent people is an ellipsis for commanding obedience, which they disobeyed.
rows.anchor: انه من الأمر وفي الكلام اضمار تقديره امرنا مترفيها بالطاعة ففسقوا هذا مذهب سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The obedience reading is illustrated by saying, I commanded you and you disobeyed me: disobedience is opposition to a command.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج ومثله في الكلام امرتك فعصيتني فقد علم ان المعصية مخالفة الأمر

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Another reading and interpretation makes the verb mean that God increased the affluent in number; Arabic usage describes abundant offspring as plentiful.
rows.anchor: كثرنا يقال أمرت الشيء وآمرته أي كثرته ومنه قولهم مهرة مأمورة

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The verb can mean that God made the affluent rulers, giving them authority.
rows.anchor: ان معنى امرنا امرنا يقال امرت الرجل بمعنى امرته والمعنى سلطنا مترفيها بالإمارة

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وابن عباس وأبي الدرداء وأبي رزين والحسن والضحاك ويعقوب
rows.claim: An extended reading, āmarnā, is reported from these readers and also means that God made the people numerous.
rows.anchor: وروى خارجة عن نافع أمرنا ممدودة مثل آمنا

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وأبو العالية والنخعي والجحدري
rows.claim: A geminated reading is transmitted for Abū ʿAmr and read by others; Ibn Qutayba interprets it as making the affluent rulers.
rows.anchor: قرأ امرنا مشددة الميم وهي رواية أبان عن عاصم وهي قراءة أبي العالية والنخعي

rows.speaker: أبو المتوكل وأبو الجوزاء وابن يعمر
rows.claim: They read amirnā with fatḥ on the hamza and kasra on the mīm, a form also glossed as increasing their numbers.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو المتوكل وأبو الجوزاء وابن يعمر أمرنا بفتح الهمزة مكسورة الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The affluent are people whose luxury and abundance have made them insolent; exegetes describe them as tyrants, powerful rulers, and kings, singled out because others follow their leaders.
rows.anchor: فهم المتنعمون الذين قد أبطرتهم النعمة وسعة العيش والمفسرون يقولون هم الجبارون والمسلطون والملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here fisq means persisting in disbelief, since fisq in disbelief is departure into its most extreme form.
rows.anchor: أي تمردوا في كفرهم لأن الفسق في الكفر الخروج إلى افحشه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The decree then fell upon the town in the form of punishment.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل وجب عليها العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word tadmīr, destruction, was explained earlier in the discussion of al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكرنا معنى التدمير في الاعراف 137

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurūn is the plural of qarn; differing definitions of qarn and the meaning of all-knowing and all-seeing were discussed in earlier commentary.
rows.anchor: وكم اهلكنا من القرون وهو جمع قرن وقد ذكرنا اختلاف الناس فيه في الانعام 6

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The warning about destroyed generations is directed at the people of Mecca.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل وهذه الاية تخويف لأهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one seeking the immediate world means a person whose deeds are aimed at worldly life; an adjective is used in place of the noun.
rows.anchor: يعني من كان يريد بعمله الدنيا فعبر بالنعت عن الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly provision hastened to such a person is explained either as worldly goods or as expansion and restriction of provision.
rows.anchor: عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء من عرض الدنيا وقيل من البسط والتقتير

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق الفزاري
rows.claim: One interpretation of those chosen to receive hastened provision is that God intends their destruction.
rows.anchor: لمن نريد هلكته قاله أبو اسحاق الفزاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God intends to hasten something for that person.
rows.anchor: لمن نريد ان نعجل له شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage rebukes people who work for worldly life: they obtain only what was allotted to them, then enter Hell in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ذم لمن اراد بعمله الدنيا وبيان انه لا ينال مع ما يقصده منها الا ما قدر له

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarīr says this verse concerns those who do not believe in resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جرير هذه الاية لمن لا يوقن بالمعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking the afterlife means seeking Paradise and performing the deeds appropriate to it; faith is required for deeds to be valid, and God accepts, rewards, and praises this striving.
rows.anchor: يعني الجنة وسعى لها سعيها أي عمل لها العمل الذي يصلح لها وانما قال وهو مؤمن لأن الايمان شرط في صحة الاعمال

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Kullan is accusative with namuddu, functioning as an alternative to kull, with the sense that God provides to both groups.
rows.anchor: كلا منصوب ب نمد هؤلاء بدل من كل والمعنى نمد هؤلاء

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: God gives worldly provision to both the righteous and the wicked; this gift means sustenance, which is not withheld from either group, while the afterlife belongs only to the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: كلا نعطي من الدنيا البر والفاجر والعطاء هاهنا الرزق والمحظور الممنوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are distinguished either in provision, with some receiving little and others much, or in both provision and deeds, with some enabled to do good and others prevented.
rows.anchor: وفيما وفضلوا فيه قولان أحدهما الرزق منهم مقل ومنهم مكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second explanation includes differences in livelihood and in success at righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: والثاني الرزق والعمل فمنهم موفق لعمل صالح ومنهم ممنوع من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition of associating another god with God addresses the Prophet but applies generally to all morally responsible people; the abandoned person has no helper, since khidhlān is withholding aid.
rows.anchor: الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمعنى عام لجميع المكلفين والمخذول الذي لا ناصر له

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The verse was revealed when people invited the Prophet to follow the religion of his forefathers.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل نزلت حين دعوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى ملة آبائه

rows.speaker: ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Qadā rabbuka means that your Lord commanded.
rows.anchor: روى ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال امر ربك

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk transmits a reading wa-waṣṣā rabbuka, also read by Ubayy and others, but Ibn al-Jawzī rejects it as contrary to consensus.
rows.anchor: الضحاك انه قال انما هي ووصى ربك

rows.speaker: أبو عمران وعاصم الجحدري ومعاذ القارئ
rows.claim: They read qaḍā with qāf, a long ḍād, hamza, and nominative form, with the Lord's name genitive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمران وعاصم الجحدري ومعاذ القارئ وقضاء ربك بقاف وضاد بالمد والهمز والرفع

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Here decree means binding duty, but it belongs to the category of command and obligation; the root notion is cutting something decisively and precisely.
rows.anchor: هذا القضاء من باب الحتم والوجوب لكنه من باب الامر والفرض وأصل القضاء في اللغة قطع الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A line mourning ʿUmar uses qaḍaytu to mean that matters were decisively settled.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر يرثي عمر قضيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to show iḥsān to parents means to be dutiful and honor them, as explained at al-Baqara 83.
rows.anchor: وأمر بالوالدين إحسانا وهوالبر والإكرام وقد ذكرنا هذا في البقرة 83

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر
rows.claim: They read yablughanna as a singular verb, predicated first of one parent and then referring to both.
rows.anchor: قرا ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر يبلغن على التوحيد

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: They read yablughāni as dual because both parents have just been mentioned; one or both is then parenthetical.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف يبلغان على التثنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readers vary the case and vocalization of uff; Zajjaj counts seven dialect forms, while excluding the form ending in yāʾ from valid recitation.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج فيها سبع لغات الكسر بلا تنوين وبتنوين والضم بلا تنوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari enumerates ten grammatical or dialectal forms of uff, while Abū Manṣūr lists related spoken variants and rejects the yāʾ form as an error.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الانباري في أف عشرة أوجه أف لك بفتح الفاء وأف بكسرها

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: One explanation of uff is dirt under the fingernail.
rows.anchor: انه وسخ الظفر قاله الخليل

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Another explanation of uff is earwax or dirt in the ear.
rows.anchor: وسخ الأذن قاله الاصمعي

rows.speaker: ثعلب
rows.claim: A further explanation of uff is a clipped fingernail.
rows.anchor: قلامة الظفر قاله ثعلب

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Uff can express contempt or belittling, from an Arabic word for scarcity.
rows.anchor: الاحتقار والاستصغار من الأفف والأفف عند العرب القلة ذكره ابن الأنباري

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Uff may be a piece of stick or reed picked up from the ground.
rows.anchor: ان الأف ما رفعته من الأرض من عود أو قصبة حكاه ابن فارس

rows.speaker: أبو منصور اللغوي
rows.claim: Abū Manṣūr explains uff as foul smell or exasperation, from blowing dust or ash away, and says it came to express anything burdensome.
rows.anchor: معنى الأف النتن والتضجر وأصلها نفخك الشيء يسقط عليك من تراب ورماد

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayd says uff and tuff originally refer to dirt on the fingers when rubbed.
rows.anchor: اصل الأف والتف الوسخ على الأصابع إذا فتلته

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Linguists distinguish ear dirt as uff and nail dirt as tuff; Arabs use both for what they dislike, find unclean, or resent.
rows.anchor: أصل الأف في اللغة وسخ الأذن والتف وسخ الأظفار فاستعملتهما العرب فيما يكره

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Another distinction makes uff nail dirt and tuff something worthless, such as ear dirt or a splinter from the ground.
rows.anchor: قد قيل إن أف وسخ الأظفار والتف الشيء الحقير نحو وسخ الأذن أو الشظية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse forbids words expressing impatience with parents in old age; one should serve them as they once cared for and served the child.
rows.anchor: لا تقل لهما كلاما تتبرم فيه بهما اذا كبرا وأسنا فينبغي ان تتولى من خدمتهما

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: He interprets not to scold them as not raising one's hand against them.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء بن أبي رباح لا تنقضي يدك عليهما

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Nahara and intahara both mean to rebuke or repel someone.
rows.anchor: نهرت الرجل وانتهرته مثل زجرته

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The prohibition is especially emphasized in old age because parents then show more behavior that irritates or harms and need more care.
rows.anchor: وانما نهى عن اذاهما في الكبر وإن كان منهيا عنه على كل حالة لأن حالة الكبر يظهر فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A noble word to parents is gentle, tender, and the best wording one can find.
rows.anchor: أي لينا لطيفا أحسن ما تجد

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: He describes the child's noble speech as that of a sinful servant to a harsh master.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن المسيب قول العبد المذنب للسيد الفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lowering the wing of humility means softening one's manner toward parents in mercy; Aṭāʾ also says the wings are the hands, which should not be raised over them.
rows.anchor: ألن لهما جانبك متذللا لهما من رحمتك إياهما

rows.speaker: أبو رزين والحسن وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة وعاصم الجحدري وابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: These readers pronounce the ḏāl in ḏull with kasra, while the majority use ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقرا أبو رزين والحسن وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة وعاصم الجحدري وابن أبي عبلة بكسر الذال

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Ḏull with ḍamma is humility before parents without servile degradation; with kasra it is the state of being tamed, as of an animal or earth.
rows.anchor: الذل ان تتذلل لهما من الذل والذل أن تتذلل ولست بذليل في الخدمة

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Lexical authorities distinguish a human who is humble from a domesticated animal described as tamed.
rows.anchor: الذل من الرجل الذليل والذل من الدابة الذلول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وعكرمة ومقاتل
rows.claim: Some held that the general prayer for mercy was abrogated as to polytheist parents by the ban on seeking forgiveness for polytheists.
rows.anchor: ذهب قوم إلى ان هذا الدعاء المطلق نسخ منه الدعاء لأهل الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects calling this abrogation: a general wording received a specification, a view also attributed to Ibn Jarir.
rows.anchor: ولا أرى هذا نسخا عند الفقهاء لأنه عام دخله التخصيص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows inward dutifulness and disobedience; a lapse is forgiven if the person did not intend disobedience.
rows.anchor: بما تضمرون من البر والعقوق فمن بدرت منه بادرة وهو لا يضمر العقوق غفر له ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣāliḥīn is explained as obedient, dutiful to parents, or repentant.
rows.anchor: أي طائعين لله وقيل بارين وقيل توابين

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: One of ten interpretations of awwāb is a Muslim.
rows.anchor: انه المسلم رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Awwāb can mean one who repents; Mujahid, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Abū ʿUbayda share this view.
rows.anchor: انه التواب رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس وبه قال مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Awwāb is the person who repents repeatedly.
rows.anchor: هو التائب مرة بعد مرة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Awwāb means one who turns back from everything God forbade; the word denotes returning.
rows.anchor: هو التواب المقلع عن جميع ما نهاه الله عنه يقال قد آب يؤوب أوبا اذا رجع

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another interpretation calls the awwāb one who glorifies God.
rows.anchor: انه المسبح رواه سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Awwāb can mean one who obeys God.
rows.anchor: انه المطيع لله تعالى رواه علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Awwāb is one who remembers a sin in private and asks God to forgive it.
rows.anchor: انه الذي يذكر ذنبه في الخلاء فيستغفر الله منه قاله عبيد بن عمير

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Awwāb is a person who turns to God with heart and deeds.
rows.anchor: انه المقبل إلى الله تعالى بقلبه وعمله قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Awwāb can mean someone who performs prayer.
rows.anchor: السابع المصلي قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن المنكدر
rows.claim: Awwāb is one who prays between sunset and nightfall.
rows.anchor: هو الذي يصلي بين المغرب والعشاء قاله ابن المنكدر

rows.speaker: عون العقيلي
rows.claim: Awwāb is one who performs the forenoon prayer.
rows.anchor: الذي يصلي صلاة الضحى قاله عون العقيلي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Awwāb is a person who sins privately and repents privately.
rows.anchor: انه الذي يذنب سرا ويتوب سرا قاله السدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: One interpretation takes relatives as a person's kin on both the father's and mother's sides.
rows.anchor: قرابة الرجل من قبل أبيه وامه قاله ابن عباس والحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their due may be kindness and maintaining kinship, necessary support when they are in need, or a bequest at death.
rows.anchor: في حقهم ثلاثة أقوال احدها ان المراد به برهم وصلتهم والثاني النفقة الواجبة

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين والسدي
rows.claim: Another view identifies the relatives as the Prophet's kin; their due is a share of the fifth, and the address is to rulers.
rows.anchor: انهم قرابة الرسول قال علي بن الحسين عليهما السلام والسدي فعلى هذا يكون حقهم إعطاؤهم من الخمس

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
rows.claim: The due of the poor and wayfarer may be obligatory alms or what is owed to them in necessity; alternatively the poor receive charity and the wayfarer hospitality.
rows.anchor: يجوز ان يكون المراد الصدقات الواجبة يعني الزكاة ويجوز ان يكون الحق الذي يلزمه اعطاؤه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
rows.claim: Waste means spending money where it has no right to be spent.
rows.anchor: انه انفاق المال في غير حق قاله ابن مسعود وابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Even spending all one's wealth for a rightful purpose is not waste, but spending a single mudd for a wrongful purpose is waste.
rows.anchor: لو انفق الرجل ماله كله في حق ما كان مبذرا ولو انفق مدا في غير حق كان مبذرا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Waste is spending outside obedience to God; the pre-Islamic Arabs slaughtered camels and squandered wealth for boastfulness and reputation, so spending should instead serve nearness to God.
rows.anchor: وكانت الجاهلية تنحر الابل وتبذر الاموال تطلب بذلك الفخر والسمعة

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Another interpretation defines waste as extravagance that destroys wealth.
rows.anchor: انه الإسراف المتلف للمال ذكره الماوردي

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: A squanderer is an excessive, corrupt, destructive spender.
rows.anchor: المبذر هو المسرف المفسد العائث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Squanderers are brothers of devils because they comply with and resemble them in disobeying God.
rows.anchor: لأنهم يوافقونهم فيما يدعونهم اليه ويشاكلونهم في معصية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is ungrateful to his Lord, denying His blessings; the verse therefore implies that the spendthrift is ungrateful for blessings.
rows.anchor: وكان الشيطان لربه كفورا أي جاحدا لنعمه وهذا يتضمن أن المسرف كفور للنعم

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: The people from whom one turns away are the previously mentioned kin, poor, and wayfarers; most say inability to give is the reason, and God's hoped-for mercy means provision.
rows.anchor: انهم الذين تقدم ذكرهم من الاقارب والمساكين وابناء السبيل قاله الاكثرون

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: For the relatives, poor, and wayfarers, one may turn away out of fear that they will spend the money on disobedience; hoped-for mercy then means their reform and repentance.
rows.anchor: والثاني خوف انفاقهم ذلك في معصية الله قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Another view identifies those addressed as polytheists, from whom the Prophet turns away because they reject him; hoped-for mercy can mean victory over them or their guidance.
rows.anchor: انهم المشركون فالمعنى واما تعرضن عنهم لتكذيبهم قاله سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about people of Muzayna who asked the Prophet for mounts; he had none, so they wept.
rows.anchor: ناس من مزينة جاؤوا يستحملون رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال لا اجد ما أحملكم عليه فبكوا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: It was also said to concern poor men such as Khabbāb, Bilāl, ʿAmmār, and Mihja, whom the Prophet could not give and so met with silence; here mercy means provision.
rows.anchor: نزلت في خباب وبلال وعمار ومهجع ونحوهم من الفقراء

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Qawlan maysūran means gentle, easy speech.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة لينا هينا وهو من اليسر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: One interpretation of the gentle speech is a good promise to help later.
rows.anchor: انه العدة الحسنة قاله ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Another interpretation is a gracious expression such as, May God provide for you and for us.
rows.anchor: انه القول الجميل مثل ان يقول رزقنا الله واياك قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
rows.claim: If the people are polytheists, the instruction means speaking to them tactfully; on this interpretation the verse may have been abrogated.
rows.anchor: انه المداراة لهم باللسان على قول من قال هم المشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it for whom He wills, arranging people's livelihood according to what He knows will benefit them.
rows.anchor: يوسع على من يشاء ويضيق انه كان بعباده خبيرا بصيرا حيث أجرى أرزاقهم على ما علم فيه صلاحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on killing children from fear of poverty was explained at al-Anʿām 151.
rows.anchor: خشية املاق قد فسرناه في الانعام 151

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers vary the form of khaṭʾan: most use kasra on khāʾ, sukūn on ṭāʾ, and hamza; other readers use the forms khaṭāʾ, khaṭaʾ, or khaṭan.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي خطءا مكسورة الخاء ساكنة الطاء مهموزة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Khiṭʾ means sin and may be synonymous with khaṭaʾ; the forms khat, khataʾ, and khataʾ are dialect variants.
rows.anchor: الخطء الإثم وقد يكون في معنى خطأ كما قالوا قتب وقتب وحذر وحذر

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Khaṭiʾtu and akhṭaʾtu are two lexical forms.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيده خطئت وأخطأت لغتان

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The long reading khaṭāʾ may be treated as the verbal noun of an otherwise unattested form khāṭaʾa, supported by a cited line.
rows.anchor: قراءة ابن كثير خطاء يجوز أن تكون مصدر خاطأ وان لم يسمع خاطأ

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Khaṭiʾa means to sin intentionally, whereas akhṭaʾa means to miss the mark unintentionally.
rows.anchor: خطئ يخطأ بمعنى أذنب وليس بمعنى أخطأ لأن اخطأ فيما لم يصنعه عمدا

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Khaṭʾ denotes sinning, while akhṭaʾa means departing from what is correct; the distinction was explained at Yūsuf 91.
rows.anchor: الخطء الإثم يقال قد خطئ يخطأ إذا أثم وأخطأ يخطئ إذا فارق الصواب

rows.speaker: أبو رزين وأبو الجوزاء والحسن
rows.claim: These readers lengthen the alif in zinā; Abū ʿUbayda says this lengthening is also used in the speech of Najd.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو رزين وابو الجوزاء والحسن بالمد قال أبو عبيدة وقد يمد الزنا في كلام اهل نجد

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq's poetry attests the long-vowel pronunciation of zināʾ.
rows.anchor: قال الفرزدق أبا حاضر من يزن

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: A further line attributed to the poet also attests the lengthened pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وقال ايضا أخضبت فعلك للزناء ولم تكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition against killing a protected soul was explained at al-Anʿām 151.
rows.anchor: ولا تقتلوا النفس التي حرم الله قد ذكرناه في الانعام 151

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Assimilating the dāl of jaʿalnā to the jīm in jaʿalnā is the better pronunciation; clear articulation is also very good, and assimilation is permitted because the tongue positions are near.
rows.anchor: الأجود إدغام الدال مع الجيم والإظهار جيد بالغ إلا أن الجيم من وسط اللسان والدال من طرف اللسان

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The slain person's walī is the relative entitled to demand the blood claim; if there is no walī, the ruler is the walī.
rows.anchor: ووليه الذي بينه وبينه قرابة توجب المطالبة بدمه فان لم يكن له ولي فالسلطان وليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One interpretation of the walī's sultan is proof or legal authority.
rows.anchor: انه الحجة قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the sultan the governor, who supports the walī and gives him justice in his right.
rows.anchor: انه الوالي والمعنى فقد جعلنا لوليه سلطانا ينصره وينصفه في حقه قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم
rows.claim: They read fa-lā yusrif with third-person yāʾ, while Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read it with second-person tāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابو عمرو وعاصم فلا يسرف بالياء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: If the warning addresses the slain person's walī, one excess is killing someone other than the killer.
rows.anchor: ان يقتل غير القاتل قاله بن عباس والحسن

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: If addressed to the walī, another excess is killing two people for one victim.
rows.anchor: أن يقتل اثنين بواحد قاله سعيد بن بن جبير

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Another excess is killing someone more socially eminent than the killer.
rows.anchor: ان يقتل اشرف من الذي قتل قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Another excess is mutilating the killer.
rows.anchor: ان يمثل قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Another excess is that the walī personally kills the killer rather than leaving execution to the ruler.
rows.anchor: ان يتولى هو قتل القاتل دون السلطان ذكره الزجاج

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A second view takes the warning to address the original killer, who must not go beyond justice by killing unjustly.
rows.anchor: ان الإشارة إلى القاتل الأول والمعنى فلا يسرف القاتل بالقتل تعديا وظلما قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة والجمهور
rows.claim: In the phrase He is supported, the pronoun may refer to the walī, supported by permission to exact retaliation.
rows.anchor: انها ترجع إلى الولي فالمعنى انه كان منصورا بتمكينه من القود قال قتادة والجمهور

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The pronoun may instead refer to the slain person, whose killer is killed in retaliation.
rows.anchor: انها ترجع إلى المقتول فالمعنى انه كان منصورا بقتل قاتله قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations refer the pronoun to the blood, which is avenged, or to the killing itself; al-Farrāʾ reports these last two readings.
rows.anchor: انها ترجع إلى الدم فالمعنى ان دم المقتول كان منصورا أي مطلوبا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on approaching an orphan's property was explained at al-Anʿām 152.
rows.anchor: ولا تقربوا مال اليتيم قد شرحناه في الانعام 152

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fulfill covenants is general: it covers duties between a servant and God and duties among people.
rows.anchor: وهو عام فيما بين العبد وبين ربه وفيما بينه وبين الناس

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Everything God commands or prohibits is part of the covenant.
rows.anchor: كل ما أمر الله به ونهى عنه فهو من العهد

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Being questioned about the covenant means being held accountable for it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أي مسؤولا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Give full measure and do not shortchange anyone.
rows.anchor: أوفوا الكيل اذا كلتم أي أتموه ولا تبخسوا منه

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read qistas with ḍamma on the qāf; other readings include kasra, two ṣāds, ṣād before ṭāʾ, or a final nūn.
rows.anchor: قسطاس بضم القاف وسينين وهذه قراءة ابن كثير ونافع وأبي عمرو وابن عامر

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read qistas with kasra on the qāf; al-Farrāʾ considers the kasra and ḍamma two dialects.
rows.anchor: كذلك إلا أن القاف مكسورة وهذه قراءة حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم

rows.speaker: أبو منصور اللغوي عن ابن دريد
rows.claim: Qistas is a balance, a Persian loan adapted into Arabic; the source records five language forms, including qistān with nūn.
rows.anchor: قسطان بالنون قرأت على شيخنا أبي منصور اللغوي عن ابن دريد قال القسطاس الميزان رومي معرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Full measure is better before God and nearer to Him, with a better eventual outcome in recompense.
rows.anchor: ذلك الوفاء خير عند الله وأقرب اليه وأحسن تأويلا أي عاقبة في الجزاء

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The root of taqfu is qiyāfa, tracing footprints; Arabic uses both qafā yaqfū and qāfa yaqūfu.
rows.anchor: أصل تقف من القيافة وهي تتبع الأثر وفيه لغتان قفا يقفو وقاف يقوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers derive the verb from qafawtu, with a vowel shift to wāw and a still qāf; Muʿādh al-Qāriʾ reads taqif from qāfa yaqūfu.
rows.anchor: واكثر القراء يجعلونها من قفوت فيحرك الفاء إلى الواو ويجزم القاف

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Reading the fāʾ still and the qāf with ḍamma treats the form as a reversal of qafā yaqfū, with the same meaning of following a trace.
rows.anchor: من قرأ باسكان الفاء وضم القاف من قاف يقوف فكأنه مقلوب من قفا يقفو

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Do not follow conjecture or guesswork; the word evokes following behind something and tracking it.
rows.anchor: لا تتبعه الظنون والحدس وهو من القفاء مأخوذ

rows.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The verse can forbid accusing anyone of something without knowledge.
rows.anchor: لا ترم أحدا بما ليس لك به علم رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عطاء عن أبيه ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Another interpretation forbids falsely claiming to have seen or heard something.
rows.anchor: لا تقل رأيت ولم تر ولا سمعت ولم تسمع رواه عثمان بن عطاء عن أبيه ابن عباس وبه قال قتادة

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: A further interpretation is that the verse forbids associating anything with God.
rows.anchor: لا تشرك بالله شيئا رواه عطاء أيضا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
rows.claim: The verse may forbid giving false testimony.
rows.anchor: لا تشهد بالزور قاله محمد بن الحنفية

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Kull is grammatically singular, but the demonstrative ulāʾika can refer collectively to people and nonhuman things; a line by Jarir attests ulāʾika for days.
rows.anchor: إنما قال كل ثم قال كان لأن كلا في لفظ الواحد وإنما قال أولئك

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The ears, eyes, and heart will be questioned about their use, warning against unlawful looking, listening, and intentions.
rows.anchor: الإشارة إلى الجوارح المذكورة يسأل العبد يوم القيامة فيما اذا استعملها

rows.speaker: الضحاك وابن يعمر
rows.claim: They read marahan with kasra on the rāʾ; al-Akhfash finds the verbal-adjective reading preferable, while al-Zajjaj considers both good and the verbal noun more emphatic.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك وابن يعمر مرحا بكسر الراء قال الأخفش والكسر أجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walking in the earth with marah means strutting arrogantly and boastfully; marah is insolent exuberance or intense joy.
rows.anchor: وتأويل الاية لا تمش في الأرض مختالا فخورا والمرح الأشر والبطر

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Marah can mean intense joy.
rows.anchor: المرح شدة الفرح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not rupturing the earth means either not cutting through it to its end or not penetrating and boring through it.
rows.anchor: فيه قولان أحدهما لن تقطعها إلى آخرها والثاني لن تنفذها وتنقبها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Your arrogance cannot tear the earth or reach the mountains in height.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس لن تخرق الأرض بكبرك ولن تبلغ الجبال طولا بعظمتك

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: A person too weak to accomplish such feats should not swagger or act proud.
rows.anchor: لا ينبغي للعاجز ان يبذخ ويستكبر

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: They read sayyiʾahu with tanwīn and without annexation, taking the phrase to mean an offense; on this reading kull refers only to the prohibited matters.
rows.anchor: سيئه منونا غير مضاف على معنى كان خطيئة

rows.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read sayyiʾuhu in annexation, masculine, making kull refer to everything previously mentioned.
rows.anchor: سيئه مضافا مذكرا فتكون لفظة كل يشار بها إلى سائر ما تقدم ذكره

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr rejected the annexed reading.
rows.anchor: وكان أبو عمرو لا يرى هذه القراءة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj calls Abū ʿAmr mistaken: the passage contains good commands as well as bad acts, so the annexed reading best includes all that preceded.
rows.anchor: وهذا غلط من أبي عمرو لأن في هذه الأقاصيص سيئا وحسنا

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda likewise argues from the passage's good commands, such as honoring parents and giving kin their due.
rows.anchor: تدبرت الآيات من قوله تعالى وقضى ربك فوجدت فيها أمورا حسنة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The unannexed reading can be explained by taking the speech to end at the statement about the best outcome, since the following prohibition is not good.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سيئة رأى أن الكلام انقطع عند قوله وأحسن تأويلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revealed wisdom refers to the preceding duties and practices: soundly established matters and comprehensive guidance encompassing all good; the meaning of driven away was explained at al-Aʿrāf 18.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى ما تقدم من الفرائض والسنن من الحكمة أي من الأمور المحكمة والأدب الجامع لكل خير

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: This rebuke concerns Arab polytheists who claimed that angels were daughters of the Merciful.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل نزلت في مشركي العرب الذين قالوا الملائكة بنات الرحمن

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Afa-aṣfākum means, Did He single you out?
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة ومعنى أفأصفاكم اختصكم

rows.speaker: المفضل
rows.claim: The verb can mean that God chose or reserved something exclusively for the addressees.
rows.anchor: وقال المفضل أخلصكم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The verb can mean that God selected the choice portion of something for the addressees.
rows.anchor: أختار لكم صفوة الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke is that people claim God chose sons for them while taking daughters for Himself, assigning themselves the superior and God the inferior.
rows.anchor: أختار لكم البنين دونه وجعل البنات مشتركة بينكم وبينه فاختصكم بالأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's repeated presentation means making matters clear through varied expression; Ibn Qutayba glosses it as directing or turning something toward someone, and the intensified form marks repetition.
rows.anchor: معنى التصريف هاهنا التبيين وذلك انه إنما يصرف القول ليبين

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر
rows.claim: They read li-yadhdhakkarū with a doubled dhāl; Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf read it with a light dhāl.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر ليذكروا مشدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering here means taking admonition and reflecting; the varied reminder only increases their flight from the truth.
rows.anchor: والتذكر الاتعاظ والتدبر وما يزيدهم تصريفنا وتذكيرنا إلا نفورا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Their flight is from the truth, as they follow falsehood.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ينفرون من الحق ويتبعون الباطل

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read the phrase taqūlūna in the second person; Ibn Kathir and Ḥafṣ read yaqūlūna in the third person.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وأبن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وابو بكر عن عاصم تقولون بالتاء

rows.speaker: الحسن وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: If rival gods existed, they would seek a way to resist God and remove His sovereignty.
rows.anchor: لابتغوا سبيلا إلى ممانعته وإزالة ملكه قاله الحسن وسعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Alternatively, they would seek a way to reach God's favor, since they are beneath Him.
rows.anchor: لابتغوا سبيلا إلى رضاه لأنهم دونه قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وأبو بكر وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read yaqūlūna in the third person; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read taqūlūna in the second person.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وأبو بكر وحفص عن عاصم يقولون بالياء

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read the verb tasbaḥ with feminine tāʾ; other readers use masculine yāʾ, which al-Farrāʾ says suits a small number of feminine or masculine subjects.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم تسبح بالتاء

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: The heavens' glorification is evidence that God is the Creator and powerful.
rows.anchor: قال العلماء والمراد بهذا التسبيح الدلالة على أنه الخالق القادر

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: One view takes the universal wording literally: everything glorifies God, even clothing, food, and a door's creaking.
rows.anchor: أنه على إطلاقه فكل شيء يسبحه حتى الثوب والطعام وصرير الباب قاله إبراهيم النخعي

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والضحاك
rows.claim: One restricted interpretation says all living things glorify God.
rows.anchor: أنه كل شيء فيه الروح قاله الحسن وقتادة والضحاك

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Another restriction includes living beings and growing plants: a tree glorifies, but a column does not; al-Hasan once said a serving tray used to glorify.
rows.anchor: الشجرة تسبح والأسطوانة لا تسبح

rows.speaker: خالد بن معدان عن المقدام بن معدي كرب
rows.claim: A report says dust glorifies until wet, a leaf while on its tree, and new clothing until it becomes dirty; each ceases when altered.
rows.anchor: إن التراب ليسبح ما لم يبتل فاذا ابتل ترك التسبيح وإن الورقة تسبح ما دامت على الشجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speaking animals' glorification is known; non-speaking animals may glorify by sound or by indicating their Maker.
rows.anchor: فأما تسبيح الحيوان الناطق فمعلوم وتسبيح الحيوان غير الناطق فجائز ان يكون بصوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three views of inanimate glorification are that it is real but known only to God, submission to God, or its pointing to its Maker and thus prompting an observer to glorify.
rows.anchor: وفي تسبيح الجمادات ثلاثة أقوال أحدها انه تسبيح لا يعلمه الا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If glorification is literal, the statement that people do not understand it addresses all people; if it means evidence of the Maker, it addresses disbelievers who fail to infer and reflect.
rows.anchor: فان قلنا إنه تسبيح حقيقة كان قوله ولكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم لجميع الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meanings of Forbearing and Forgiving were explained at al-Baqara 225.
rows.anchor: وقد شرحنا معنى الحليم و الغفور في البقرة 225

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: One view says the veil is the coverings placed on their hearts.
rows.anchor: ان الحجاب هو الأكنة على قلوبهم قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: The veil is something that hides the Prophet from their sight; the verse was revealed about people who harmed him while he recited, including Abū Sufyān, al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, Abū Jahl, and Umm Jamīl, whom God prevented from seeing him.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنها نزلت في قوم كانوا يؤذون رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قرأ القرآن قال الكلبي

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God prevented them from harming the Prophet.
rows.anchor: انه منع الله عز وجل إياهم عن أذاه حكاه الزجاج

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Mastūr may mean a covering that actively conceals; Arabic sometimes uses a passive form with active meaning, as in mashʾūm and maymūn.
rows.anchor: أنه بمعنى ساتر قال الزجاج وهذا قول أهل اللغة قال الأخفش وقد يكون الفاعل في لفظ المفعول

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Alternatively, the veil is hidden from the addressees so they cannot see it.
rows.anchor: أن المعنى حجابا مستورا عنكم لا ترونه ذكره الماوردي

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: If the veil is a seal on their hearts, it is literally concealed from sight and remains passive in meaning.
rows.anchor: إذا قيل الحجاب هو الطبع على قلوبهم فهو مستور عن الأبصار فيكون مستورا باقيا على لفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coverings on their hearts were explained at al-Anʿām 25.
rows.anchor: أكنة أن يفقهوه قد شرحناه في الأنعام 25

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God alone in recitation means saying there is no god but God; turning away on their backs means departing in aversion.
rows.anchor: يعني قلت لا إله إلا الله وأنت تتلو لقرآن ولوا على أدبارهم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Nufūr means turning on their heels; as a plural it parallels quʿūd and julūs.
rows.anchor: أي على أعقابهم نفورا وهو جمع نافر بمنزلة قاعد وقعود

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Nufūr can be an infinitive meaning flight, or a plural meaning those who flee.
rows.anchor: تحتمل مذهبين أحدهما المصدر فيكون المعنى ولوا نافرين نفورا والثاني ان يكون نفورا جمع نافر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The people turning away may be devils.
rows.anchor: أنهم الشياطين قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Alternatively, those turning away are the polytheists.
rows.anchor: انهم المشركون وهذا مذهب ابن زيد

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: At the Prophet's instruction, ʿAlī prepared a meal for Quraysh leaders; the Prophet recited the Qur'an and called them to monotheism, but they whispered that he was a sorcerer or bewitched.
rows.anchor: أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عليا عليه السلام ان يتخذ طعاما ويدعو إليه أشراف قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition bi- in yastamiʿūna bihi is extra; the sense is that they listen to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أي يستمعونه والباء زائدة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Najwā is an infinitive from nājaytu that is also used as a description of people, as in the expression you are grief.
rows.anchor: هي مصدر من ناجيت واسم منها فوصف القوم بها والعرب تفعل ذلك

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The phrase means they were people engaged in private conversation.
rows.anchor: والمعنى وإذ هم ذوو نجوى

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Masḥūr may mean a person who has been bewitched and lost his reason.
rows.anchor: قاله أبو صالح نع ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets masḥūr as deceived or deluded; Ibn Qutayba prefers this because magic means trickery and the next verse says they made comparisons.
rows.anchor: مخدوعا مغرورا قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Masḥūr can mean a being with lungs, since every breathing creature eats; the accusation would distinguish Muhammad from angels, who do not eat.
rows.anchor: له سحر أي رئة وكل دابة أو طائر أو بشر يأكل فهو مسحور

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labīd's line calling people al-musaḥḥar attests the sense of being fed or sustained.
rows.anchor: قال لبيد فان تسألينا فيم نحن

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays uses nusaḥḥaru to mean that people are fed, sustained, or beguiled by food and drink.
rows.anchor: وقال امرؤ القيس أرانا مرصدين لأمر

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: He favors Mujahid's meaning of deceived: the comparison makes sense if the Quraysh meant the Prophet was tricked by people who taught him.
rows.anchor: والقول قول مجاهد أي مخدوعا لأن السحر حيلة وخديعة

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The opponents set out comparisons by likening the Prophet to a magician, poet, or madman, and thus went astray.
rows.anchor: بينوا لك الأشباه حتى شبهوك بالساحر والشاعر والمجنون فضلوا عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says they cannot find a way to make their accusations against the Prophet sound valid.
rows.anchor: لا يجدون سبيلا إلى تصحيح ما يعيبونك به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they cannot find guidance because their hearts have been sealed.
rows.anchor: لا يستطيعون سبيلا إلى الهدى لأنا طبعنا على قلوبهم

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: They cannot follow the path of truth because it feels burdensome to them, like saying one cannot bear to look at someone one dislikes.
rows.anchor: لا يأتون سبيل الحق لثقله عليهم ومثله قولهم لا أستطيع أن انظر إلى فلان

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the first hamza with a following still yāʾ and no lengthening, as he does throughout the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير أيذا بهمزة ثم يأتي بياء ساكنة من غير مد

rows.speaker: قالون عن نافع والكسائي
rows.claim: Qālūn does not interrogate the second hamza; al-Kisāʾī also treats the second as declarative but uses two hamzas in the first.
rows.anchor: كذلك روى قالون عن نافع الا ان نافعا كان لا يستفهم في أينا

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: They use two hamzas for both interrogative words; Ibn ʿĀmir has one hamza in idhā and two in a-innā, with a long interval.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة بهمزتين في الحرفين جميعا

rows.speaker: الفراء ومجاهد
rows.claim: Rufāt can mean dust or crumbs and has no singular form, like other collective words for fragments.
rows.anchor: انه التراب ولا واحد له فهو بمنزلة الدقاق والحطام قاله الفراء وهو مذهب مجاهد

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Rufāt can mean bones before they have been crushed; it also means broken fragments.
rows.anchor: أنه العظام مالم تتحطم والرفات الحطام قاله أبو عبيدة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Rufāt means dust or anything crushed and broken; jadīd here means renewed.
rows.anchor: الرفات التراب والرفات كل شيء حطم وكسر وخلقا جديدا في معنى مجددا

rows.speaker: ابن عمر وابن عباس والحسن والأكثرون
rows.claim: The thing considered too great in their hearts is death.
rows.anchor: أنه الموت قاله ابن عمر وابن عباس والحسن والاكثرون

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Another view identifies it as heaven, earth, and mountains.
rows.anchor: انه السماء والأرض والجبال قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: It can mean anything in God's creation that they regard as immense.
rows.anchor: ما يكبر في صدوركم من كل ما استعظموه من خلق الله تعالى قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to become stone or iron is either a challenge to change their state, followed by assurance that God can still kill them, or an invitation to imagine themselves as harder than stone before He destroys them.
rows.anchor: فعنه جوابان أحدهما إن قدرتم على تغير حالاتكم فكونوا حجارة أو اشد منها

rows.speaker: الأحوص
rows.claim: A line by al-Aḥwaṣ illustrates the second reading: imagine yourself a solid stone if you have renounced pleasure and youth.
rows.anchor: فكن حجرا من يابس الصخر جلمدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objectors accepted that God created them but denied resurrection; the One who began their creation can bring them back to life.
rows.anchor: وهؤلاء قوم اعترفوا ان الله خالقهم وجحدوا البعث فأعلموا ان الذي ابتدأ خلقهم هو الذي يحييهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: They shake their heads in disbelief and mockery.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة يحر كونها تكذيبا واستهزاء

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The verb anghaḍa describes moving the head up and down.
rows.anchor: يقال أنغض رأسه إذا حركه إلى فوق وإلى أسفل

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: It is the motion of someone who despairs or thinks something impossible; the same root describes a loose tooth.
rows.anchor: المعنى يحر كونها كما يحرك الآيس من الشيء والمستبعد له رأسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question about when it will occur refers to resurrection, which God says is near.
rows.anchor: يعنون البعث قل عسى ان يكون قريبا أي هو قريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God summons people from their graves with the final blast; they hear the call and answer it.
rows.anchor: يعني من القبور بالنداء الذي يسمعكم وهو النفخة الأخيرة فتستجيبون أي تجيبون

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Isrāfīl stands on the rock in Jerusalem and calls decayed bones, flesh, hair, and veins to come for judgment; the dead hear and hurry to him.
rows.anchor: يقوم إسرافيل على صخرة بيت المقدس يدعو أهل القبور في قرن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جريج وابن زيد
rows.claim: Bihamdihi can mean that the resurrection occurs by God's command.
rows.anchor: بأمره قاله ابن عباس وابن جريج وابن زيد

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: People emerge from their graves saying, Glory and praise be to You.
rows.anchor: يخرجون من القبور وهم يقولون سبحانك وبحمدك قاله سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Bihamdihi can mean with knowledge of and obedience to God; al-Zajjaj takes their response as acknowledgment that He is their Creator.
rows.anchor: ان معنى بحمده بمعرفته وطاعته قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Another view says they answer by praising God, not themselves.
rows.anchor: تجيبون بحمد الله لا بحمد أنفسكم ذكره الماوردي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb taẓunnūna may mean being certain, or it may retain its ordinary sense of supposing.
rows.anchor: في هذا الظن قولان أحدهما انه بمعنى اليقين والثاني انه على اصله

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: One view says they consider their stay short because the forty-year interval between blasts is a period of rest when punishment ceases.
rows.anchor: بين النفختين ومقداره أربعون سنة ينقطع في ذلك العذاب عنهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: They think worldly life was short compared with the long afterlife.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا لعلمهم بطول اللبث في الآخرة قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: They consider the grave stay short because they have emerged into something more severely punishing.
rows.anchor: في القبور قاله مقاتل فعلى هذا انما قصر اللبث في القبور عندهم لأنهم خرجوا إلى ما هو أعظم عذابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes address the verse to believers: they answer in praise of God's kindness and regard the grave stay as brief because they were not punished there.
rows.anchor: ذهب بعض المفسرين إلى أن هذه الآية خطاب للمؤمنين لأنهم يجيبون المنادي وهم يحمدون الله

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: One occasion of revelation was that Meccan polytheists verbally and physically harmed the Prophet's companions, who complained to him.
rows.anchor: أن المشركين كانوا يؤذون أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة بالقول والفعل

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Another report says an unbeliever insulted ʿUmar, who was about to attack him when this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: أن رجلا من الكفار شتم عمر بن الخطاب فهم به عمر رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: If the addressees are polytheists, the best response is to say, May God guide you.
rows.anchor: تقول له يهديك الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say believers were told to speak well to polytheists before fighting them, and the instruction was later abrogated by the sword verse.
rows.anchor: امروا بهذه الآية بتحسين خطاب المشركين قبل الأمر بقتالهم ثم نسخت هذه الآية بآية السيف

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Another view addresses Muslims, telling them to use the best expressions with one another.
rows.anchor: انهم المسلمون قاله ابن جرير والمعنى وقل لعبادي يقول بعضهم لبعض التي هي أحسن

rows.speaker: مبارك عن الحسن
rows.claim: Rather than returning an equivalent phrase, the best response is to pray, May God have mercy on you and forgive you.
rows.anchor: روى مبارك عن الحسن قال التي هي أحسن أن يقول له مثل قوله ولكن يقول له يرحمك الله

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: The jussive construction yaqūlū is parallel to the construction yuqīmū al-ṣalāh.
rows.anchor: وقوله يقولوا مثل قوله يقيموا الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan provokes conflict between people and is plainly their enemy.
rows.anchor: أي يفسد ما بينهم والعدو المبين الظاهر العداوة

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: If the addressees are believers, God may rescue them from the Meccans or punish them by empowering those people over them.
rows.anchor: إن يشأ يرحمكم فينجيكم من أهل مكة وإن يشأ يعذبكم فيسلطهم عليكم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: For believers, mercy can mean repentance and punishment can mean persisting in sins.
rows.anchor: إن يشأ يرحمكم بالتوبة أو يعذبكم بالإقامة على الذنوب قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: If the addressees are polytheists, mercy may mean guidance to faith and punishment may mean dying in disbelief.
rows.anchor: أو إن يشأ يعذبكم فيميتكم على الكفر قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
rows.claim: Another reading concerns a drought: God knows who among the polytheists will believe; He may lift the famine as mercy or leave it as punishment.
rows.anchor: لما نزل القحط بالمشركين فقالوا ربنا اكشف عنا العذاب إنا مؤمنون

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The disjunctive aw conveys the breadth of what God can do, comparable to giving someone the choice to sit with al-Hasan or Ibn Sirin.
rows.anchor: و أو هاهنا دخلت لسعة الأمرين عند الله تعالى وأنه لا يرد عنهما

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Wakīl can mean a guarantor who is answerable for them.
rows.anchor: كفيلا تؤخذ بهم قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Wakīl may mean a guardian or master.
rows.anchor: حافظا وربا قاله الفراء

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Wakīl can mean a guarantor responsible for their guidance, with power to reform their hearts.
rows.anchor: كفيلا بهدايتهم وقادرا على إصلاح قلوبهم ذكره ابن الأنباري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes considered the disclaimer that the Prophet is not their guardian abrogated by the sword verse.
rows.anchor: وذهب بعض المفسرين إلى أن هذا منسوخ بآية السيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the inhabitants of heaven and earth because He created them; He guides and misguides as He wills, and favors prophets with wisdom and knowledge.
rows.anchor: لأنه خالقهم فهدى من شاء وأضل من شاء وكذلك فضل بعض النبيين على بعض وذلك عن حكمة منه وعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage illustrates prophetic distinctions: Adam was created by God's hand, Idris raised, Noah made ancestor of descendants, Abraham God's intimate friend, Moses spoken to, Jesus a spirit, Solomon given great dominion, and Muhammad elevated above the heavens and forgiven.
rows.anchor: فخلق آدم بيده ورفع إدريس وجعل الذرية لنوح واتخذ إبراهيم خليلا وموسى كليما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the favored ones may be recipients of scriptures, since the passage closes by mentioning the Psalms given to David.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المفضلون أصحاب الكتب لأنه ختم الكلام بقوله وآتينا داود زبورا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: One occasion of revelation concerns Arabs who worshipped jinn; the jinn accepted Islam while their Arab worshippers did not know.
rows.anchor: أن نفرا من العرب كانوا يعبدون نفرا من الجن فأسلم الجن والنفر من العرب لا يشعرون

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Another occasion concerns polytheists who worshipped angels, claiming they would intercede, during a seven-year drought.
rows.anchor: أن المشركين كانوا يعبدون الملائكة ويقولون هي تشفع لنا عند الله فلما ابتلوا بالقحط سبع سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supposed deities cannot remove harm from people or transfer it elsewhere.
rows.anchor: فلا يملكون كشف الضر عنكم ولا تحويلا له إلى غيركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The referents of those invoked may be the converted jinn or the angels mentioned in the preceding discussion.
rows.anchor: أحدها أنهم الجن الذين أسلموا والثاني الملائكة وقد سبق بيان القولين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A third view includes Jesus, Ezra, angels, the sun, and the moon among the referents.
rows.anchor: أنهم المسيح وعزير والملائكة والشمس والقمر قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most interpret yadʿūna as the polytheists worshipping the beings they invoke as gods.
rows.anchor: يعبدون أي يدعونهم آلهة وهذا قول الأكثرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, yadʿūna means those beings themselves pray to God seeking nearness; on this parsing the verb refers to them and yabtaghūna completes the sentence, whereas the first reading resumes with the worshippers.
rows.anchor: انه بمعنى يتضرعون إلى الله في طلب الوسيلة وعلى هذا يكون قوله يدعون راجعا إلى أولئك

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وأبو عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: They read tadʿūna in the second person; Ibn al-Anbari says this links the verb to the previous statement that the invoked beings cannot remove harm.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وابن عباس وأبو عبد الرحمن تدعون بالتاء

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: With third-person yadʿūna, Arabic can shift from direct address to an absent subject when the meaning remains clear.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ يدعون بالياء قال العرب تنصرف من الخطاب إلى الغيبة إذا أمن اللبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meaning of wasīla was explained at al-Māʾida 35.
rows.anchor: وقد فسرنا معنى الوسيلة في المائدة 35

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Ayyuhum aqrab can be parsed as a subject with predicate: they seek a means to God through whoever is nearest to Him.
rows.anchor: أن يكون أيهم مرفوعا بالابتداء وخبره أقرب ويكون المعنى يطلبون اليه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Alternatively, ayyuhum is appositional to the plural subject of yabtaghūna: each seeks the nearest means to God through righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: أن يكون أيهم أقرب بدلا من الواو في يبتغون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In wa-in min qarya, in means mā, that is, not a town exists except that God will destroy it before the Resurrection or punish it severely.
rows.anchor: إن بمعنى ما والقرية الصالحة هلاكها بالموت والعاصية بالعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A righteous town's destruction means death, while a disobedient town is punished; the book is the Preserved Tablet and mastūr means written.
rows.anchor: والكتاب اللوح المحفوظ والمسطور المكتوب

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Meccans asked for Ṣafā to become gold and the mountains to be moved so they could farm; the Prophet chose to give them more time rather than grant a sign that could bring destruction if rejected.
rows.anchor: ان أهل مكة سألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يجعل لهم الصفا ذهبا وأن ينحي عنهم الجبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second occasion was mentioned under the request to make the Qur'an move mountains, at al-Raʿd 31; God withheld the requested signs because earlier peoples were punished after denying such signs.
rows.anchor: قد ذكرناه عن الزبير في قوله ولو أن قرآنا سيرت به الجبال الرعد 31

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not send the requested signs so that these people would not reject them and be destroyed, following the established practice of punishing nations who denied signs they demanded.
rows.anchor: وسنة الله في الأمم أنهم إذا سألوا الآيات ثم كذبوا بها عذبهم

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Mubṣira means a clear sign; Ibn al-Anbari also allows a causative sense, visible to its observers, attributed figuratively to the she-camel.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أي بينة يريد مبصرا بها

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The she-camel may be called seeing because she made the observers see; this is figurative attribution, like telling someone not to let oneself see them when the meaning is not to appear.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون مبصرة ويصلح أن يكون المعنى مبصر مشاهدوها فنسب اليها فعل غيرها تجوزا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with fatḥ on mīm and ṣād makes mubṣira an intensive description of how clearly the she-camel manifested the sign.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ مبصرة بفتح الميم والصاد فمعناه المبالغة في وصف الناقة بالتبيان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Fa-ẓalamū bihā means they denied the she-camel sign.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس فجحدوا بها

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Alternatively, their wrongdoing was committed through or against the she-camel.
rows.anchor: بها كان ظلمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends signs only to frighten people into taking warning.
rows.anchor: أي نخوف العباد ليتعظوا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: One interpretation of the signs sent as warnings is widespread death.
rows.anchor: أنها الموت الذريع قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: The signs may be prophetic miracles or signs of divine punishment that warn people away from sins.
rows.anchor: معجزات الرسل جعلها الله تعالى تخويفا للمكذبين والثالث آيات الانتقام تخويفا من المعاصي

rows.speaker: الإمام أحمد
rows.claim: The signs can be the changes in a person's life from childhood to youth, maturity, and old age, which should prompt reflection on the end of life.
rows.anchor: تقلب أحوال الإنسان من صغر إلى شباب ثم إلى كهولة ثم إلى مشيب ليعتبر
